summary.headline: Natco Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue at Rs 1,090.4 crore and EBITDA margin 30.4%; management guides FY27 revenue of Rs 775-800 crore-range driver commentary and higher international sales.
summary.overview: Consolidated total revenue was Rs 1,090.4 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 794 crore in Q1 but down from Rs 1,463 crore a year earlier, which management attributed to lower lenalidomide revenue. EBITDA including other income was Rs 310 crore (30.4% margin) and consolidated PAT was Rs 202.6 crore versus Rs 206.5 crore in Q1. The company completed a rights issue, repaid its acquisition-related debt, and raised its stake in Adcock Ingram to 49%. Management said FY27 revenue could be slightly under Rs 800 crore-equivalent growth, with Q4 expected to be weaker, and flagged lumpy earnings from one-off and high-risk assets.

financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 794 crore QoQ; down from Rs 1,463 crore YoY
vs Rs 206.5 crore in Q1 FY27
After purchase price allocation adjustment; Q1 was higher on flu season
Includes some semaglutide stocking; management sees base of Rs 130-135 crore
Standalone about 27%; FY guidance standalone 27-27.2%, consolidated 29-30%

segments.name: International formulations
segments.commentary: Drove the QoQ revenue increase; management guided base international sales of about Rs 850-900 crore with one-time sales lifting consolidated figures near Rs 1,000 crore. Brazil, Middle East and Canada expected to drive rest-of-world growth.

segments.name: Domestic formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 145 crore in Q2 including semaglutide stocking; management called Rs 135 crore the repeatable base and said base business grew about 20%. Management expects 15-20% growth next year.

segments.name: Adcock Ingram (associate)
segments.commentary: Stake raised by 13.25% in July 2026 to 49%. Management expects about Rs 55-60 crore annual share of profit after amortisation and one-time charges, versus Rs 29.2 crore in Q2.

segments.name: Crop Health Sciences (agrochemicals)
segments.commentary: Marginal profit in Q2 (about Rs 0.1 crore); management expects about Rs 20 crore loss for the year in the demerged business and 15-20% growth in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance from prior quarter reiterated as Rs 3,400-3,500 crore by the earlier framing; management said it could do better and expects roughly Rs 775-800 crore of a related metric; Q3 looks good, Q4 weaker.
R&D spend guided at 8-10% of top line, about Rs 300-350 crore for FY27 versus over Rs 400 crore last year; Q3 expected higher, Q4 moderate.
FY28 revenue growth of about 10-15% indicated informally; formal FY28 guidance to be given near fiscal year-end.
Debt fully repaid after rights issue; no loans outstanding as of the call date.
Crop Health Sciences demerger filing with SEBI delayed by 4-6 months; mid-calendar 2027 now targeted.
Capex of about Rs 300 crore in H1; maintenance-plus-expansion run-rate around Rs 350-400 crore a year.
Dividend policy to remain steady; no change.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about Rs 300 crore, above normal run-rate of Rs 350-400 crore a year, for Chennai and Hyderabad-area API blocks, formulation upgrades and a new oncology line (Silesite, just started production).
Cephalosporin-type/internal line to be ready next financial year.
Pipeline launches expected in next few quarters: carfilzomib (lowest strength with sole first-to-file), another first-to-file US product, and Olaparib launch expected.
South Africa (Adcock) multiple product filings made; regulatory approval expected in 1.5-2 years.
demand_pricing: Indian semaglutide: Natco estimated about 5-6% volume share and about 3% value share; vial sells about Rs 1.2-1.5 crore/month, pen about Rs 0.5 crore/month.
Management described semaglutide generic pricing as very poor with unprofitable participants; long-run upside depends on market growth.
Government price cut on semaglutide expected to have limited impact as distributor margins were compressed.
Pomalidomide first-to-file was shared with five to six other filers, causing steep price erosion and a limited earnings bump.
US business is strong only where competition is limited; management said rest-of-world is more stable than US.
Brazil growth was about 66% YoY in Q2; management indicated H1 Brazil revenue about Rs 300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin in Q1 and Q2 sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current operating margin run-rate is sustainable based on current trajectory, with earnings diversified across Adcock, Brazil and base US business.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Adcock Ingram profit run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 12-14 million USD per annum at 100%, implying Rs 55-60 crore consolidated share after amortisation, with Q1 seasonally highest.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for rights issue proceeds and further M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds mainly used to repay debt taken for Adcock; the rest retained for working capital and a possible acquisition, which management is pursuing but has not closed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the eGenesis investment monetisable?
qa_highlights.answer: Stake is single-digit percent; about USD 25 million invested. Options include Indian licence and possible IPO; data clarity expected in next 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was R&D spend up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly R&D, plus FDA facility fees, program fees and some legal costs; R&D is milestone-driven and lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: India DSO expected at 90-120 days; standalone tax rate about 27% for FY, consolidated about 29-30%.

risks_watch: Lumpiness of earnings from one-time orders and high-risk assets (eGenesis, pipeline); management acknowledged market reluctance to pay for such risk.
Semaglutide generic price erosion in India and unprofitability of market participants.
Q4 FY27 expected to be weaker; FY28 guidance deferred to year-end.
Crop Health Sciences demerger timing slipped to mid-calendar 2027 pending SEBI filing.
Pending US FDA queries on semaglutide approval; Ozempic-related exclusivity not yet confirmed.
Pending acquisition, timing and terms unclear; management declined to give valuation targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Adcock, Brazil and base-business momentum, but defensive and evasive on stock valuation, M&A targets, FY28 guidance and semaglutide regulatory status, deferring details to year-end.
key_quotes: I think the market appreciates more steady earnings, which are low-risk and they give a higher multiple for that.
US is a tough bet, I think US is the most important market in our genetics business.
I think it'll be between 775 to 800 is what I feel.
So I think, relatively the rest of the world is the most stable business compared to US, but you can't ignore US.

adds.what: Silesite new oncology line (just started production)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 PAT of Rs 775-800 crore (raised) and FY28 revenue growth of 10-15% indicated informally, backed partly by Silesite oncology line starting, Rs 300 crore H1 capex, pipeline launches (carfilzomib, Olaparib) and Adcock stake raise, but no firm capacity numbers or order book sizing; quarter revenue down 25.5% YoY on lenalidomide decline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says the current operating margin run-rate (Q2 EBITDA margin 30.4%, Q1 PAT Rs 206.5 crore, Q2 PAT Rs 202.6 crore) is sustainable, but Q4 is guided weaker and R&D is 8-10% of top line (Rs 300-350 crore FY27 vs over Rs 400 crore last year).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Silesite oncology line just started production and a Cephalosporin-type/internal line is planned for next financial year, with H1 FY27 capex of about Rs 300 crore against a Rs 350-400 crore annual run-rate.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Brazil revenue up 66% YoY to Rs 121 crore with H1 Brazil guided near Rs 300 crore, base domestic business up about 20%, and Adcock profit share guided at Rs 55-60 crore a year vs Rs 29.2 crore in Q2; offset by lenalidomide decline (revenue Rs 1,090.4 crore vs Rs 1,463 crore YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; capex is held at the Rs 350-400 crore annual run-rate with new lines (Silesite, Cephalosporin-type) already planned, so a fresh announcement is only conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management raised FY27 PAT guidance to Rs 775-800 crore and said it could do better, with Q3 looking good and the company's pitch that base international sales are Rs 850-900 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY27 is explicitly expected to be weaker, and earnings are lumpy from one-time orders, pomalidomide-type price erosion and high-risk assets (eGenesis, pipeline), so the Q4 shortfall could cut the full-year outlook.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pipeline launches guided for the next few quarters: carfilzomib (lowest strength, sole first-to-file), another first-to-file US product, and Olaparib; the Silesite line has just started production.

rows.label: Indian semaglutide: US FDA queries and Ozempic exclusivity unresolved
rows.why: Pending US FDA queries on semaglutide approval; Natco holds about 5-6% Indian volume share (about 3% value), and management deferred regulatory details to year-end.

rows.label: Crop Health Sciences demerger
rows.why: SEBI filing delayed 4-6 months; demerged business guided at about Rs 20 crore loss for FY27 with 15-20% growth next year.

rows.label: South Africa (Adcock) product approvals
rows.why: Multiple product filings made in South Africa with regulatory approval expected in 1.5-2 years, a longer-dated volume driver.

tone.note: Management was confident on Adcock, Brazil, base-business momentum and raised FY27 PAT guidance to Rs 775-800 crore, but was evasive on valuation, M&A targets, FY28 formal guidance and semaglutide regulatory status; analysts' questions focused on margin sustainability, Adcock run-rate and the eGenes
